questions.q: Per-plan decision thresholds were chosen on the validation set and then applied to the test set. Why not choose them on the test set?
options: The test set is too small to score
Tuning on the test set leaks information, so its results would no longer be an honest estimate
Thresholds can only be computed on validation data by definition
SageMaker forbids reading test data
questions.explain: Choosing settings on the test data makes the reported test numbers optimistic. Selection happens on validation; the untouched test set is used once for the final estimate.

questions.q: After applying per-plan thresholds, overall recall rose from 0.556 to 0.726 and overall precision fell from 0.708 to 0.609. What is the fair summary?
options: The change is strictly better with no downside
The change is strictly worse and should be reverted
Metrics on a test set cannot be compared
More churners are caught but more customers who would have stayed are flagged; the value depends on business costs
questions.explain: Lowering thresholds trades precision for recall. Whether it pays off depends on what a retention call costs versus a lost customer.

questions.q: Which item does NOT belong on a model card described in this lesson?
options: Known limits such as weak recall on weekly plans
What the model must not be used for
Test metrics and the monitoring plan
The AWS account's root password
questions.explain: A model card describes purpose, data, metrics, limits, misuse and monitoring. Credentials never belong in any project document.

questions.q: Which is the best way to handle what you could not verify without an AWS account?
options: State plainly that endpoint behavior, latency, IAM and container compatibility were not verified
Omit it so the project looks complete
Report invented latency numbers
Claim the illustrative code was tested
questions.explain: Candor about what was and was not verified builds credibility. Never present unrun cloud code or invented numbers as tested.

questions.q: Which cleanup step prevents ongoing charges from a real-time deployment?
options: Deleting only the local Python files
Rejecting the model version in the registry
Deleting the monitoring schedule and the endpoint (plus its config and model), then confirming in billing
Turning off your laptop
questions.explain: Endpoints and recurring monitoring jobs bill while they exist. Deleting the serving resources and checking billing is the reliable fix.
